title: SparkLend deprecates a collateral asset by stacking Frozen state with 0% LTV while keeping a nonzero liquidation threshold
content:
Two parameters that look redundant are in fact a wind-down tool. LTV is "the maximum percentage of the value of collateral that borrowers can borrow against their collateral" (A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.1.4) — it gates *new* borrowing. The liquidation threshold is "the maximum debt a borrower can owe as a percentage of their collateral before their position is considered under-collateralized" (.1.5) — it gates *destruction of existing* positions.

Because they are independent, LTV can be driven to zero while the liquidation threshold stays above zero. New borrowing against the asset stops immediately; open positions remain alive and can be repaid or unwound in the borrower's own time.

The GNO configuration (A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.2.1.1) is this pattern fully assembled: `LTV: 0%`, `Liquidation Threshold: 25%`, `Borrowing: No`, `Slope 1: 0%`, `Slope 2: 0%`, `Reserve State: Frozen` — where Frozen means "all activities may occur except for supplying and borrowing" (.1.14). Every entry point is shut and every exit is open. Dai shows a more aggressive variant: `LTV: 0%` with `Liquidation Threshold: 0.01%`, leaving effectively no collateral value at all.

The alternative — setting the liquidation threshold to zero, or moving straight to `Paused`, where "no activities may occur" — would mass-liquidate or trap every existing borrower for an administrative decision they had no part in. The three-state Reserve State plus the LTV/threshold gap is how the protocol retires an asset without expropriating the users who trusted it, and reading the two numbers together is the only way to tell a deprecation from a healthy market.
description: LTV governs new borrowing power and the liquidation threshold governs when existing positions die, so the gap between them is the runway given to legacy borrowers.
